share.description: Its weight in the traffic mix (default 1). Shares are relative: 7 and 3 mean 70% and 30%.

deadline.description: Deadline propagation. Pass down: the request carries the time when the user gives up. Each hop waits only until then; a request that has expired is dropped in the queue, so no wasted work; no retries after it expires. (default off)

Adaptive LIFO: FIFO normally, LIFO when the queue has not emptied for 100 ms. (default fifo)

coldFactor.description: Cold start factor. How many times normal the processing time is when a new machine just comes up. (default 3)

replicaDelayMs.description: Replication lag (ms). After the primary writes, how long the write takes to reach a replica (network, batched sends). This time plus the replica queue and apply time is the replication lag. Reading a replica during this window gives a stale read. (default 0)

maxLagMs.description: Max replication lag (ms). Reads skip a replica that lags more than this (like a proxy max replication lag check). If all replicas lag too much, read the primary. 0 means no check. (default 0)

failoverS.description: Failover time (s). How long from a primary failure until a replica takes over: detect, confirm, pick the new primary, reconnect. All writes fail in that time. RDS Multi-AZ instances take about 60–120 seconds; Multi-AZ clusters about 20–35 seconds. (default 90)

fencing.description: Fence the old primary. In a network partition, the replicas' side thinks the primary is down and promotes a new one. The old primary still runs, and users on its side still write to it: both sides take writes (split brain), and the data diverges when the partition ends. With fencing (like STONITH or an epoch token), the old primary refuses writes as soon as the new one is up. (default off)

readYourWrites.description: Read your writes. A user who reads right after writing, from a replica that has not received the write yet, does not see their own write (read-your-writes fails). rywWindowMs.description: Primary-read window (ms). How long after a write the reads go to the primary. Make it longer than the usual replication lag. (default 2000)

locks.description: Row locks. A write to a row (a key) must first take that row's lock. Writes to a hot key run one at a time: writes waiting for the lock hold a connection, and latency and queues grow. That key takes at most 1 ÷ (write time + lock hold) writes per second. (default off)

lockHoldMs.description: Lock held after the write (ms). How long the transaction keeps the lock after the write before it commits (other queries in the transaction, or the application calls another service inside it). (default 0)

writeMs.description: Write time (ms). Processing time for one write. Write a number (mean in ms), or { mean, cv }; cv is the coefficient of variation, 1 = exponential, 0 = fixed. (default mean 10 ms, cv 1)

anyOf.description: Mean in ms (cv keeps its default).

queueLimit.description: Max queue. How many requests each instance queues. When full, reject right away (queue_full). 0 means no queueing. (default 500)

errorRate.description: Error rate. Share of messages that fail at random after processing. (0–1, default 0)

readFrom.description: Read source. Where read queries go. (default replicas)

replicaApplyRatio.description: Replica write-apply cost. For each write to the primary, every replica also spends "write time × this ratio" applying it. So replicas cannot save write volume. 0 means not counted (and stale reads are not computed). (0–1, default 0.3)

replicaDelayMs.description: Replication lag (ms). After the primary writes, how long the write takes to reach a replica (network, batched sends). This time plus the replica queue and apply time is the replication lag. Reading a replica during this window gives a stale read. (default 0)

maxLagMs.description: Max replication lag (ms). Reads skip a replica that lags more than this (like a proxy max replication lag check). If all replicas lag too much, read the primary. 0 means no check. (default 0)

localReplicas.description: Replicas in the primary's region. With a replica region, the first replicas stay in the primary's region and the others go to the replica region. A read goes to a replica in the caller's region first. (default 0)

failover.description: Automatic failover. When the primary fails, the replica that is furthest along becomes the primary. Replication is asynchronous: writes the primary acknowledged but had not sent to this replica yet are lost. Needs read replicas and a replica apply cost above 0 (to track replication). (default off)

failoverS.description: Failover time (s). How long from a primary failure until a replica takes over: detect, confirm, pick the new primary, reconnect. All writes fail in that time. RDS Multi-AZ instances take about 60–120 seconds; Multi-AZ clusters about 20–35 seconds. (default 90)

fencing.description: Fence the old primary. In a network partition, the replicas' side thinks the primary is down and promotes a new one. The old primary still runs, and users on its side still write to it: both sides take writes (split brain), and the data diverges when the partition ends. With fencing (like STONITH or an epoch token), the old primary refuses writes as soon as the new one is up. (default off)

readYourWrites.description: Read your writes. A user who reads right after writing, from a replica that has not received the write yet, does not see their own write (read-your-writes fails). When on, reads within the window after a write go to the primary. Cost: more reads on the primary. (default off)

rywWindowMs.description: Primary-read window (ms). How long after a write the reads go to the primary. Make it longer than the usual replication lag. (default 2000)

locks.description: Row locks. A write to a row (a key) must first take that row's lock. Writes to a hot key run one at a time: writes waiting for the lock hold a connection, and latency and queues grow. That key takes at most 1 ÷ (write time + lock hold) writes per second. (default off)

lockHoldMs.description: Lock held after the write (ms). How long the transaction keeps the lock after the write before it commits (other queries in the transaction, or the application calls another service inside it). (default 0)

maxDepth.description: Max depth. How many messages it can hold. When full, writes are rejected (queue_full). (default 100000)

enqueueMs.description: Write latency (ms). Time to write and get an ack. Write a number (mean in ms), or { mean, cv }; cv is the coefficient of variation, 1 = exponential, 0 = fixed. (default mean 2 ms, cv 0.5)

anyOf.description: Mean in ms (cv keeps its default).

delivery.description: Delivery mode. At most once: if the worker fails or crashes, the message is lost. At least once (like SQS): delete only when the worker succeeds; if it fails or is too slow, the message comes back after the visibility timeout and may be processed twice. (default at_most_once)

visibilityTimeoutMs.description: Visibility timeout (ms). How long a message stays hidden after it is handed to a worker. If it is not done (or it fails) in that time, the message shows up again for another worker. If this is shorter than the process time, messages get processed twice. (default 30000)

maxReceives.description: Max receive count (DLQ). When a message is taken this many times without success, it moves to the dead-letter queue (DLQ) and is not retried. 0 means no DLQ, so it retries forever. (default 0)

messageTtlS.description: Message retention (s). Drop a message (expire it) if it is still not processed after this long. 0 means keep it forever. (default 0)

ordering.description: Ordering. FIFO (like SQS FIFO or a Kafka partition): messages of one group (one key) are handed out one at a time; the next one goes only when the previous one is done, dropped or moved to the DLQ. When one is stuck (slow, or a poison message retried again and again), its whole group waits (head-of-line blocking). (default standard)

groups.description: Message groups. With FIFO, messages are split into this many groups by key (like message groups or partitions). Fewer groups block each other more often, and also limit how many messages are worked on at once. (default 16)

errorRate.description: Error rate. Share of messages that fail at random after processing. (0–1, default 0)

poisonRate.description: Poison message ratio. Share of messages with bad content that fail on every attempt. Use it with the queue's at-least-once setting and the DLQ to see the effect. (0–1, default 0)

calls.description: How to call the downstream. With several downstreams, call them in sequence or in parallel. (default sequential)

outbox.description: Message after write (outbox). When a write saves to a database and sends a message to a queue: off, the two are separate calls, and when one succeeds and the other fails they disagree (dual write). On, the message is written to an outbox table in the same transaction as the data; a relay then sends it to the queue and retries until it gets there. The request succeeds when the database write does. (default off)

outboxRetryMs.description: Outbox retry interval (ms). How long the relay waits after a failed send before it sends again. (default 1000)

autoscale.description: Autoscaling. When on, "Instances" is the minimum count. Every so often it checks the average busy rate: too busy adds machines, too idle removes machines. A new machine takes requests only after its boot time, and it is slower right after it comes up (cold start). (default off)

maxInstances.description: Max instances. Upper limit for autoscaling. (default 10)

targetUtil.description: Target utilization. Target average utilization per instance. Instances needed = current instances × utilization ÷ target (no change if within 10%). (0–1, default 0.6)

scaleEveryS.description: Check interval (s). How often to check how busy it is and decide to add or remove. Cloud autoscaling on 1-minute metrics checks about once a minute; the Kubernetes HPA every 15 seconds. (default 60)

scaleDownS.description: Scale-down window (s). To remove instances, every check in this window must need fewer; it then removes down to the most any check in the window needed. Like the Kubernetes HPA scale-down stabilization window (300 seconds by default): it keeps a short dip from removing instances that are needed again right away. 0 means remove as soon as they are not needed. (default 300)

bootS.description: Boot time (s). After deciding to add an instance, how long until it takes requests (start a VM, pull the image, pass the health check). A new VM takes about 1–3 minutes; a container on an existing node only seconds. (default 120)

warmS.description: Warm-up time (s). After a new machine comes up, how long the processing time takes to fall linearly from the cold-start multiplier back to normal (JIT, connection pool, local cache). 0 means no warm-up. (default 20)

coldFactor.description: Cold start factor. How many times normal the processing time is when a new machine just comes up. (default 3)

provisioned.description: Provisioned environments. Environments ready from the start and never reclaimed (provisioned concurrency). Requests that use them have no cold start. They count toward the concurrency limit. (default 0)

id.description: Optional. Default: "<from>-><to>", plus ":read", ":write" or ":boot" when filtered.

from.description: Unique id. Letters, digits, _ and -. Max 48 chars.

to.description: Unique id. Letters, digits, _ and -. Max 48 chars.

on.description: Which requests it carries. This edge carries reads only, writes only, or both. "Only at boot": a new autoscaled instance calls it once while booting (get config, register, pull the image) and goes live only when every such call succeeds; requests do not take it. "Control plane": the autoscaler, automatic database failover and DNS failover call it before each decision (get metrics, ask a coordination service); when it fails they are blind and do not act this time. Requests do not take it either. (default all)

weight.description: Weight. When a node picks one of several edges, it picks by weight. (default 1)

latencyMs.description: Network latency (one way) (ms). Edges from Users default to 20 ms (internet), other edges to 0.5 ms (same data center). (default 0.5)

timeoutMs.description: Timeout (ms). How long the caller waits at most. 0 means no limit. After a timeout the downstream still finishes the work (wasted). (default 0)

retries.description: Retry count. Max retries after a failure. Rate limits (429) and an open circuit breaker are not retried. (default 0)

backoffMs.description: Retry backoff base (ms). Before retry n, wait a random 0 to base × 2^(n−1) ms (full jitter). (default 50)

retryBudget.description: Retry budget. In the last 10 s, how many times the first-call count the retries on this edge can reach (Google suggests 0.1 = 10%). Above that, no retry and the call reports failure right away. 0 means no limit. (default 0)

throttleK.description: Adaptive throttling K. Client-side throttling (Google SRE adaptive throttling). Over the last 10 s the caller counts requests sent and accepts (successes). A new call fails locally, without being sent, with probability max(0, (requests − K × accepts) ÷ (requests + 1)). K = 2 is the book's suggestion; a smaller K rejects earlier. 0 turns it off. (default 0)

bulkhead.description: Bulkhead (max concurrent calls). How many calls over this connection each caller instance may have in flight at the same time (a bulkhead). When it is full, the call fails at once (bulkhead full) instead of tying up more threads. So a slow dependency can hold only these slots, not the whole instance. 0 = no limit. (default 0)

hedgeMs.description: Hedged request (ms). When a read has no reply after this long, send a second copy (hedged request); the first success counts. Usually set to the p95 latency: about 5% more requests cut the tail latency. The losing copy still runs to the end downstream. Reads only (sending a write twice is not safe). 0 means off. (default 0)

fanout.description: Fan-out (copies sent at once). Send each call to this many copies of the target at once; the call is done when they are back (scatter-gather). Sharded database: this many shards (a search asks every shard). Database: this many of the primary and replicas (a write goes to each copy itself). Other nodes: this many different instances. More than there are means all of them. The more copies, the more likely one is slow, so the tail latency grows. 0 means one copy. (default 0)

quorum.description: Quorum (copies to wait for). With fan-out, answer as soon as this many copies succeed, without waiting for the rest (a quorum, as in Cassandra or DynamoDB: 2 of 3 copies). When too many fail to reach this number, the call fails. The copies not waited for still run to the end. 0 means wait for all. (default 0)

connectMs.description: Connection setup (ms). How long opening a new connection takes (TCP + TLS handshakes; across regions often several round trips). A connection stays open for the next call (keep-alive) and closes when idle too long; more calls at once, or the first call after an idle spell, pay this first. 0: not modelled. (default 0)

keepAlive.description: Connection reuse (keep-alive). Off: every call pays the connection setup time. Only works when "Connection setup" is above 0. (default on)

idleS.description: Idle close after (s). A connection idle this long is closed; the next call opens a new one. Only works when "Connection setup" is above 0. (default 60)

fallback.description: Fallback (degraded response). When a call over this connection finally fails (retries used up, timeout, circuit open, bulkhead full), the caller answers with a fallback response instead (for example a default recommendation list): the request still succeeds, but counts as a degraded response. Use it for dependencies that are not essential. (default off)
